title: Talking to Claude: Conversations That Work

questions.prompt: A chat went wrong three messages ago. What's usually the best move?

options.text: Edit the message where it went off course, which creates a separate branch
Keep adding corrections on top of the bad turns
Delete your account and start over
Switch to the most powerful model and repeat the same message

questions.explanation: Editing an earlier message creates a separate branch of the chat, removing the bad turns instead of stacking fixes on them.

questions.prompt: Anthropic recommends explicitly giving Claude permission to say "I don't ____" to reduce made-up answers.
questions.explanation: Allowing Claude to admit uncertainty is one of the simplest ways to reduce hallucinations.

questions.prompt: Which prompts ask for honest critique rather than agreement? Select all that apply.

options.text: List the three weakest points in this plan.
Give me the strongest argument against my position.

questions.explanation: Asking for weaknesses, counterarguments, and marked guesses invites honest analysis. A leading question signals the answer you want.

items.text: Refine until it's right, then ask for the final format
Ask for a first version with the key context

questions.explanation: Good conversations ask with context, react specifically, and refine until the result is right.

questions.prompt: Match each situation to the best move.

pairs.left: Answer is close but needs tweaks
One section of a long draft is off
pairs.right: Highlight it and use Edit with Claude

pairs.left: Material you reuse in many chats

questions.explanation: Follow-ups suit small tweaks, Edit with Claude targets sections, new chats keep context focused, and Projects hold reusable material.

questions.prompt: What is the "interview me first" pattern?

options.text: Asking Claude to ask you clarifying questions before it drafts
Asking Claude to pretend to be a job interviewer
Uploading your résumé before every chat

questions.explanation: For bigger tasks, asking Claude to interview you first collects context you might forget, so the result fits your real situation.
